correctness.rationale: The original ladder metric d((i,r),(j,s))=|i-j|+|r-s| makes every distance-two edge preserve parity i+r, and a given parity induces a P_n^2 on the n columns. Ordinary domination of each path square is the claimed exact-distance-two condition (selected vertices cover themselves); a radius-2 interval has at most five vertices and centers with consecutive gaps at most five and endpoint bounds c1<=3, cm>=n-2 cover the path. For minimum m centers, two deficits 3-c1, cm-(n-2) lie in {0,1,2}, m-1 interior deficits 5-(c_{j+1}-c_j) in {0..4}, and their telescoping sum is 5m-n. The mapping is bijective, including n=1,2,3,4, so coefficient extraction, square, and fixed-e degree 2e leading coefficient 1/(e!)^2 follow. Independent direct exhaustive subset enumeration of both ladder rows n=1..7 agreed; no infinite inference from those tests.

value.rationale: PASS: exact multiplicities and the five-residue polynomial law for minimum-cardinality distance-two domination in a natural, infinite width-two grid family are a complete enumerative classification. Counts of optimizers may be used to compare boundary effects and resilience, and are not implied by merely knowing gamma_h; the parity decomposition explains the mathematical structure rather than an arbitrary finite slice.

final_claim: For every n>=1, exact-distance-two domination of P_n square K_2 has optimum 2ceil(n/5); the number of individually-labelled minimum sets equals ([t^(5m-n)](1+t+t^2)^2(1+t+...+t^4)^(m-1))^2. The five residue classes have prescribed polynomial growth and n multiple of 5 uniquely realizes its optimum.
limitations: Limited to open width-two ladders and exact graph distance two; no cylinder, width-three, longer hop radius or nonminimal-set enumeration.
